full_text_en:
Guiding Case No. 256: Chongqing Mou Industrial Co., Ltd. v. Chongqing Mou Construction Engineering Co., Ltd. and Pan Mou — execution implementation case

(Adopted by the Judicial Committee of the Supreme People's Court and released on April 7, 2025)

Keywords
execution/execution implementation/large number of parking spaces/owners' priority/sale in separate lots

Execution Implementation Gist

When the people's court disposes of a large number of parking spaces planned for vehicle parking within a building zone, it may, in accordance with Article 276 of the Civil Code of the PRC, while lawfully protecting the legitimate rights and interests of creditors, first satisfy the needs of the owners of the residential community. The court shall comprehensively consider factors such as the nature of the parking spaces involved, the ratio of parking spaces to residential units in the community, and the legitimate rights and interests of the parties, and formulate a feasible disposal plan, such as sale in separate lots.

Basic Facts

In the dispute over a sales contract between Chongqing Mou Industrial Co., Ltd. and Chongqing Mou Construction Engineering Co., Ltd. and Pan Mou, the Chongqing Pilot Free Trade Zone People's Court rendered Civil Judgment (2021) Yu 0192 Min Chu No. 442 on January 7, 2021, ordering Chongqing Mou Construction Engineering Co., Ltd. (hereinafter "Chongqing Mou Construction Company") to pay Chongqing Mou Industrial Co., Ltd. (hereinafter "Chongqing Mou Industrial Company") the purchase price of RMB 4,330,500 and corresponding capital occupation fees of RMB 1,266,900; and ordering Pan Mou to bear joint and several suretyship liability for the above debts of Chongqing Mou Construction Company. As the judgment debtors, Chongqing Mou Construction Company and Pan Mou, failed to perform the obligations determined in the effective legal document within the prescribed period, the judgment creditor, Chongqing Mou Industrial Company, applied to the Chongqing Pilot Free Trade Zone People's Court for compulsory enforcement on March 18, 2022.

During the enforcement proceedings, the Chongqing Pilot Free Trade Zone People's Court first seized a total of 73 parking spaces owned by the judgment debtor Pan Mou, located in a certain residential community in Jiangbei District, Chongqing. The residential community where the parking spaces at issue are located was completed in 2004, comprising five buildings with a total of 445 residential units. The ratio of residential units to parking spaces was approximately 1:0.3. All 73 parking spaces are parking spaces planned for vehicle parking within the building zone and are currently leased and in use. The parking spaces at issue were purchased by the judgment debtor Pan Mou in a single transaction in 2009. Pan Mou is not currently an owner of the residential community. After the parking spaces were seized, the judgment debtors still failed to perform their obligations, and Chongqing Mou Industrial Company applied to the Chongqing Pilot Free Trade Zone People's Court for disposal.

In accordance with the legislative intent of Article 276 of the Civil Code, to first satisfy the needs of owners while also ensuring the smooth auction of the parking spaces at issue, the Chongqing Pilot Free Trade Zone People's Court decided to prioritize the disposal method of sale in separate lots over the method of sale as an entirety and further refined the specific implementation plan. Specifically: (1) The auction was conducted for owners of the residential community, with each household eligible to bid for only one parking space. If any parking spaces remained unsold, a second auction was conducted for unspecified bidders; (2) Owners who were tenants of the parking spaces and met the bidding qualifications had the preemptive right to purchase the parking spaces they rented under the same conditions.

Execution Result

On June 15, 2022, the Chongqing Pilot Free Trade Zone People's Court issued Enforcement Ruling (2022) Yu 0192 Zhi No. 737-8, ordering the auction of the 73 parking spaces. During the auction conducted for the owners of the residential community, 61 parking spaces were sold, with an average sale price of RMB 85,300. The remaining parking spaces were all sold during the auction conducted for unspecified bidders, with an average sale price of RMB 84,600. After the sales, the people's court issued auction sale rulings and notices to assist in enforcement, completing the transfer procedures for the corresponding parking spaces. The auction proceeds, after deducting the relevant taxes and fees, were all paid to the judgment creditor.

Execution Reasoning

The key to lawful and standardized enforcement in this case lies in how to dispose of the large number of parking spaces at issue.

1. The disposal of parking spaces shall first satisfy the needs of the owners. Article 276 of the Civil Code of the PRC provides: "Parking spaces and garages planned for vehicle parking within a building zone shall first satisfy the needs of the owners." This provision reflects the legislative value orientation of giving priority protection to the rights and interests of owners. This judicial disposal involves a large number of parking spaces. Therefore, in accordance with the above legislative intent, the court shall comprehensively consider factors such as the nature of the parking spaces at issue, the ratio of parking spaces to residential units in the community, and the legitimate rights and interests of the parties, and formulate a reasonable disposal plan. This must achieve the maximization of property value and lawfully protect the legitimate rights and interests of creditors, while also implementing the spirit of the relevant provisions of the Civil Code and lawfully protecting the legitimate rights and interests of the numerous owners of the residential community.

2. Regarding the issue of whether to sell the parking spaces at issue as an entirety or in separate lots. In this case, the ratio of residential units to parking spaces in the community was approximately 1:0.3, indicating a shortage of parking spaces, and all the parking spaces to be auctioned were currently leased and in use by owners of the community. From the perspective of first satisfying the needs of owners, it was appropriate to adopt the method of sale in separate lots for the disposal of the parking spaces at issue. If the disposal were conducted as an entirety, typically only one bidder would succeed in the bid, and even if that bidder were an owner, it would be difficult to protect the preemptive purchase rights of numerous tenants of the parking spaces, and the demand for parking space purchases by numerous owners without parking spaces would be difficult to satisfy.

3. Regarding the scope and order of bidders. The "first satisfy the needs of the owners" stipulated in Article 276 of the Civil Code includes not only the owners' rights to preemptive purchase, preemptive lease, and preemptive use of parking spaces but also implies that when the reasonable needs of owners are not satisfied, the parking spaces cannot be arbitrarily disposed of to third parties other than owners. Nevertheless, on the basis of "first satisfying the needs of the owners," it should be permitted to sell the parking spaces to third parties other than owners. This is conducive to lawfully protecting the legitimate rights and interests of the prevailing parties and avoids causing unnecessary impact on the rights and interests of the judgment debtor. Therefore, in the specific auction process, owners of the residential community were given priority to participate in the bidding. After the conclusion of the auction process, if there were unsold parking spaces, a second auction was conducted for unspecified bidders other than owners, thereby balancing the protection of the legitimate rights and interests of the owners of the residential community, the prevailing parties, and the judgment debtor.

Relevant Legal Provision

Article 276 of the Civil Code of the PRC
